props.heading: What we check before we list
props.intro: The same six things on every property. If one fails, we tell the owner why and do not list it.

items.title: Lalpurja and trace map
items.text: The ownership certificate matches the owner, the plot number and the area on the ground.

items.title: Road access
items.text: We measure the road ourselves. Most new houses in the valley need at least 20 ft to get a building permit.

items.title: Naksha pass
items.text: An approved building plan, and a completion certificate for finished houses.

items.title: Land tax receipts
items.text: Paid up to this year at the ward and the malpot office.

items.title: No bank loan on it
items.text: A letter from the bank if the property was ever mortgaged.

items.title: Guthi and tenancy
items.text: No guthi claim, no mohi tenant, no court case against the plot.

props.heading: From a viewing to the malpot office
props.intro: A typical house sale in the valley takes four to eight weeks. This is how it goes with us.

image.alt: A hand holding up house keys in an open doorway

items.label: Week 1
items.title: Viewing
items.text: We meet you at the gate, walk the plot and the road, and hand you copies of the papers to take away.

items.label: Week 2
items.title: Your own checks
items.text: Show the papers to your lawyer or engineer. We arrange a second visit with them at no charge.

items.label: Weeks 3 to 4
items.title: Agreement and advance
items.text: A written agreement with the price, the advance and the date of transfer, signed in front of witnesses.

items.label: Weeks 4 to 8
items.title: Transfer at malpot
items.text: We book the date, go with both sides, and hand over the keys the day the new lalpurja is issued.

props.heading: Selling? We come and look first
props.body:
Suman visits, reads your papers and walks the road with you. If there is a problem, we tell you what fixing it takes, whether you list with us or not.

We photograph the house on a clear morning, write a plain listing and show it only to buyers who have told us their budget.

items.q: Can I get a bank loan on these homes?
items.a: Most of them, yes. Every listing has the papers banks ask for. We can introduce you to the loan desks we work with, but the choice of bank is yours.

items.q: Do you sell land outside the valley?
items.a: No. We only list in the north and south of the valley, where we can visit every plot ourselves.
The buyer pays the government registration fee at the malpot office. Rates change with the budget; we give you the current figure before you sign.

items.q: Can I see the papers before a viewing?
items.a: Yes. Ask and we send copies of the lalpurja, the trace map and the naksha on Viber or email.

pages.title: Buying
pages.seoTitle: Buying a home in Kathmandu, step by step · Nilkantha Homes
pages.seoDescription: How buying a house or land works, the papers you should see, and how we help at the malpot office. Free for buyers.

props.title: Buying a home with us
props.text: Free for buyers. We show you the papers first, go with you to every visit, and stand beside you at the malpot office.

image.alt: A hand holding up house keys in an open doorway

props.eyebrow: No fee is ever asked of a buyer

items.title: Tell us what you want
items.text: Area, size, road, budget, and whether you need a bank loan.

items.title: See the papers
items.text: Copies of the lalpurja, trace map and naksha for every home you like, before you visit.

items.title: Visit
items.text: We book viewings together, usually on a Saturday morning.

items.title: Agree and pay the advance
items.text: A written agreement with the price, advance and transfer date.

items.title: Transfer
items.text: At the malpot office, with both sides and their witnesses. The keys change hands the same day.

props.heading: Papers you will see
props.intro: Ask for any of these at any time.

items.title: Lalpurja
items.text: The land ownership certificate, in the seller’s name.

items.title: Trace map
items.text: The plot on the cadastral map, with its number and neighbours.

items.title: Naksha pass and completion
items.text: The approved plan and the certificate that the house matches it.

items.title: Tax receipts
items.text: Land and house tax, paid to this fiscal year.

items.title: Char killa
items.text: A ward letter confirming the four boundaries and the road.

items.title: Bank clearance
items.text: If the property was ever mortgaged, the letter that it is free.

items.q: I live abroad. Can I still buy?
items.a: Yes, through a family member with a power of attorney (akhtiyarnama) registered in Nepal. We walk them through each step and send you photos and papers at every stage.
Ten to twenty per cent at the agreement, the rest at transfer. It is written into the agreement, with what happens to it if either side pulls out.

items.q: Do you help with the loan?
items.a: We give the bank the papers it needs and introduce you to loan officers, but we take no commission from banks.

image.alt: A sunny living room with a sofa and a balcony door onto the city

props.heading: What we do for a seller
props.body:
Suman visits, reads your papers and walks the road. If something is missing, a tax receipt or a completion certificate, we tell you how to get it and how long it takes.

Then we photograph the house on a clear morning, write a plain listing with the real size and road width, and send it to buyers already on our list before it goes on the website.

  • No photos or listing until the papers are checked
  • Every offer passed to you in writing
  • We go with you to the malpot office
